documents.title: Generative AI Statements for Syllabi
documents.stance_why: The page 'recommends instructors establish a course policy' and gives 'three versions of a policy reflecting varying levels of acceptable GenAI use', so the university sets no single rule and hands the decision to instructors through tiered templates (restrictive, less restrictive, College of Business).
tiers: More restrictive: no AI at any stage
More restrictive: AI only with advance permission and citation
Less restrictive: cite any AI use
Less restrictive: cite, mark quotes, report prompts and validation
College of Business: no AI-generated work unless the assignment says so
documents.summary: Teaching-center page with sample syllabus statements ranging from a ban to citation-based permission, plus a College of Business policy and three citation style examples. Instructors choose and adapt a statement.

documents.unit: Center for Teaching, Learning, and Assessment (CTLA)
documents.title: OHIO Faculty Course AI Policies and Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The page is a CTLA collection of faculty-contributed course policies plus generic restrictive and less restrictive options; the instructor 'recommends instructors establish a course policy' and the samples range from 'strictly prohibited' answers-only use to 'expected to use them', so no single university rule is set and the choice sits with instructors.
tiers: Faculty-contributed sample course policies (encouraged, limited, or prohibited AI)
documents.summary: A page of faculty sample AI policies from Chemistry, Management, Education, Sociology, English, Music History and others, showing permissive, limited and restrictive approaches with disclosure and reflection requirements. It closes with CTLA generic syllabus options. Most statements are examples, not university rules.
